items.followUp: Write any two characteristics of kingdom Protista.

rubric.why: One correct characteristic of Monera is required.
rubric.description: States a valid characteristic of kingdom Monera.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct characteristic.

rubric.why: A second correct characteristic completes the response.
rubric.description: States a second valid characteristic of kingdom Monera.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct correct characteristic.

modelAnswer: Organisms of kingdom Monera are unicellular and prokaryotic.
They lack a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

items.followUp: Name any two factors that threaten biodiversity.

rubric.why: Any one major cause of extinction earns this mark.
rubric.description: Names one major cause of species extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid cause.

rubric.why: A second distinct cause is needed for full credit.
rubric.description: Names a second major cause of species extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct valid cause.

modelAnswer: Major causes of species extinction include habitat destruction and overhunting.
Other causes include pollution, climate change, and the introduction of invasive species.

items.followUp: Name the two main phases of the cell cycle.

accept: between one cell division and the next
from one cell division to the next
rubric.why: The cell cycle is defined by the repeating events between successive divisions.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as the series of events between successive cell divisions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Naming its main phases adds the required textbook detail.
rubric.description: Names the main phases of the cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying interphase and the mitotic phase.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the series of events that occurs in a cell from one cell division to the next.
It consists of interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).

items.followUp: What is the difference between DNA and a gene?

rubric.why: Chromatin is the less condensed form found when the cell is not dividing.
rubric.description: Describes chromatin as an uncoiled, thread-like material, typically in a non-dividing cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct description of chromatin.

rubric.why: Chromosomes are the condensed form of chromatin, especially visible during cell division.
rubric.description: Describes chromosomes as condensed structures visible during cell division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct contrasting description of chromosomes.

modelAnswer: Chromatin is the long, thin, uncoiled form of DNA and proteins in a non-dividing cell.
Chromosomes are the condensed, compact form of chromatin, visible during cell division.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a tumour and cancer.

rubric.why: Benign tumours remain local and do not invade or spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.description: States that a benign tumour is localized and does not invade or spread.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct behaviour of a benign tumour.

rubric.why: Malignant tumours invade tissues and may spread to distant parts of the body.
rubric.description: States that a malignant tumour invades and/or spreads to other parts of the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct behaviour of a malignant tumour.

modelAnswer: A benign tumour remains localized and does not invade surrounding tissues or spread to other parts of the body.
A malignant tumour is cancerous; it invades surrounding tissues and can spread to other parts of the body (metastasis).

items.followUp: What is synapsis, and when does it occur in meiosis?

rubric.why: Chiasmata are the visible contact points between homologous chromosomes during meiosis.
rubric.description: Defines chiasmata as contact points between homologous chromosomes or their chromatids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of chiasmata.

rubric.why: Crossing over involves exchange between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.description: Defines crossing over as the exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of crossing over.

modelAnswer: Chiasmata are the points where homologous chromosomes remain attached during prophase I of meiosis.
Crossing over is the exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

items.followUp: How does carbon dioxide concentration affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Light is a limiting factor at low intensity, so increasing it raises the photosynthesis rate.
rubric.description: States that increasing light intensity increases the rate of photosynthesis at first.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct initial effect of increasing light intensity.

rubric.why: Once light is no longer limiting, another factor limits the rate.
rubric.description: States that the rate eventually levels off at high light intensity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the plateau at high intensity.

modelAnswer: As light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, provided light is a limiting factor.
At high light intensity the rate reaches a maximum and levels off because another factor becomes limiting.

items.followUp: State lactic acid fermentation and give one organism in which it occurs.

rubric.why: Alcoholic fermentation takes place without oxygen.
rubric.description: States that alcoholic fermentation is an anaerobic process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the absence of oxygen.

rubric.why: Fermentation produces ethanol and carbon dioxide; yeast commonly carries it out.
rubric.description: Identifies the products of alcoholic fermentation or the organism that performs it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming ethanol and carbon dioxide, or yeast.

modelAnswer: Alcoholic fermentation is the anaerobic breakdown of glucose, usually by yeast, producing ethanol, carbon dioxide, and energy.
